# Share kit

Single purpose: ready-to-post copy for launching Git Guide, one block per channel. Paste, adjust nothing but the mood, post. Written for Amey Thakur to post as himself.

## The one-liner

> Every Git and GitHub answer in one place: type what you want to do, or paste the error Git printed, and get the exact commands with a danger level and an undo for each. No ads, no trackers, works offline.

## Show HN

Research note: post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 10 AM Eastern. The personal-story form outperforms the technical description. Cross-post to Reddit and LinkedIn the same day; momentum in one window is what reaches the trending lists.

**Title:**

> Show HN: Git Guide, every Git answer with a danger level and its undo

**Body:**

> Four of the ten highest-voted Stack Overflow questions ever are Git questions. After years of answering the same ones for teammates, I built the resource I kept wishing existed: one page where you type what you want to do, or paste the exact error Git printed, and get the command, how dangerous it is, and how to undo it.
>
> Everything is plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JS on GitHub Pages: no framework, no build step, no trackers, works offline. The whole knowledge base is JSON served raw, with an llms.txt, so scripts and agents can use it too. Modern Git first: switch and restore, force-with-lease, worktrees, rerere.
>
> https://amey-thakur.github.io/GIT-GUIDE/

## LinkedIn

> Git runs nearly every codebase on earth, yet four of the ten most-asked programming questions in history are Git questions. People do not lack tutorials; they lack the right command at the moment they need it, and the confidence that running it is safe.
>
> So I built Git Guide: type what you want to do in plain language, or paste the error Git just printed, and get the exact commands. Every one carries a danger level (safe, rewrites history, destructive) and its own undo.
>
> Inside: an interactive model of how Git actually works, a guided rescue for any mess, every common error decoded, a complete GitHub chapter from your first repository to branch protection, and a printable cheatsheet. It works the same on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, and AWS, and it works offline.
>
> Free, open source, MIT. If it saves you once, star it so it can find the next person: https://github.com/Amey-Thakur/GIT-GUIDE
>
> https://amey-thakur.github.io/GIT-GUIDE/

## Reddit (r/git, r/programming, r/learnprogramming)

**Title:**

> I built a Git guide where every command shows its danger level and its undo

**Body:**

> You type what you want to do ("undo the last commit", "committed a secret") or paste the exact error Git printed, and it gives the commands with a badge: safe, rewrites history, or destructive, plus how to undo each one. There is also an interactive diagram of where code actually lives, a guided rescue wizard, and a printable cheatsheet. Plain HTML and vanilla JS, no trackers, works offline. Feedback welcome; missing questions get added through Discussions.
>
> https://amey-thakur.github.io/GIT-GUIDE/

## Answering people, anywhere

Every answer and every error has its own link. When someone asks a Git question in a thread, chat, or review, link them the exact fix:

> https://amey-thakur.github.io/GIT-GUIDE/#undo-last-commit
> https://amey-thakur.github.io/GIT-GUIDE/errors.html#publickey-denied

This is the quiet growth channel: one precise link at the right moment beats any launch post.
